name: movements-062
prompt:
Create beautiful ORIGINAL FORMA exercise art in a clean modern illustrated fitness manual style. Exactly FOUR columns and THREE rows, 12 equal cells, landscape 1536x1024. Each cell white with generous margins; no labels, letters, logos, borders or watermarks. Varied fully clothed adult athletes, charcoal/gray sportswear with a small lime-green accent. Correct anatomy (two arms, two legs), plausible support and weight-bearing, detailed accurate equipment, subtle shadows. Every cell is an EXACT distinct movement/variation matching its description. Show ONE clear representative working position per cell; do not show duplicate athletes, extra limbs, arrows or overlapping phases. Keep the entire athlete and apparatus inside own cell. Never swap freeweights, benches, grips or variations. Read each guide to choose a physically correct pose. Cell positions are mandatory:
Row 1 column 1: Pause Hack Squats. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Hack Squats but with a 1-2s pause at the bottom of the movement. This makes sure that there is no more elastic energy stored in the muscles.

Row 1 column 2: Paused Squats. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: Use the same technic as your normal squat. Except that you make a pause at the bottom of the squat for about 1-2 seconds, in other words a bit longer than your normal squat.

Row 1 column 3: Pelvic Tilt Into Bridge. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Lie down with your feet on the floor, heels directly under your knees. Lift only your tailbone to the ceiling to stretch your lower back. (Don't lift the entire spine yet.) Pull in your stomach. To go into a bridge, lift the entire spine except the neck.

Row 1 column 4: Pendelay Rows. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: Back excercise with a barbell with a starting position which is in a bent over position with the back paralell to the ground. The barbell is on the ground at chest level.For the movement grab the barbell at shoulder width grip and pull towards your chest without losing the bent over position and without moving anything but your arms

Row 2 column 1: Peroneals Stretch. Equipment: Specialty equipment. Exercise guide: In a seated position, loop a belt, rope, or band around one foot. This will be your starting position. With the leg extended and the heel off of the ground, pull on the belt so that the foot is inverted, with the inside of the foot being pulled towards you. Hold for 10-20 seconds, and then switch sides.

Row 2 column 2: Peroneals-SMR. Equipment: Foam roller. Exercise guide: Lay on your side, supporting your weight on your forearm and on a foam roller placed on the outside of your lower leg. Your upper leg can either be on top of your lower leg, or you can cross it in front of you. This will be your starting position. Raise your hips off of the ground and begin to roll from below the knee to above the ankle on the side of your leg, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other leg.

Row 2 column 3: Perpendicular Unilateral Landmine Row. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: Using a landmine attachment with the barbell running at 90 degrees to either side, hinge slightly at the hips and grip the barbell by the plate sleeve. Raise the barbell to chest height, with your upper arm parallel to the floor at the top of the movement.

Row 2 column 4: Physioball Hip Bridge. Equipment: Exercise ball. Exercise guide: Lay on a ball so that your upper back is on the ball with your hips unsupported. Both feet should be flat on the floor, hip width apart or wider. This will be your starting position. Begin by extending the hips using your glutes and hamstrings, raising your hips upward as you bridge. Pause at the top of the motion and return to the starting position.

Row 3 column 1: Pike Push Ups. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Push Up performed from a pike position (optional to have feet elevated).

Row 3 column 2: Pin Bench Press BB. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: * Set security pins to about the height of your sticking point * Lower the bar, rest on the pins for 1s while holding tension * Move bar up with maximum force

Row 3 column 3: Pin OHP. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: * Set security pins to the height of your lower chin * Rest bar on pins keeping tension * Raise bar over head

Row 3 column 4: Pin Presses. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: Pin presses remove the eccentric phase of the bench press, developing starting strength. They also allow you to train a desired range of motion. The bench should be set up in a power rack. Set the pins to the desired point in your range of motion, whether it just be lockout or an inch off of your chest. The bar should be moved to the pins and prepared for lifting. Begin by lying on the bench, with the bar directly above the contact point during your regular bench. Tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulder off the bench and retract them, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Use your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Maintain this tight body position throughout the movement. You can take a standard bench grip, or shoulder width to focus on the triceps. The bar, wrist, and elbow should stay in line at all times. Focus on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart. Drive the bar up with as much force as possible. The elbows should be tucked in until lockout. Return the bar to the pins, pausing before beginning the next repetition.

cells.title: Pin Presses
cells.guideText:
Pin presses remove the eccentric phase of the bench press, developing starting strength. They also allow you to train a desired range of motion.

The bench should be set up in a power rack. Set the pins to the desired point in your range of motion, whether it just be lockout or an inch off of your chest. The bar should be moved to the pins and prepared for lifting.

Begin by lying on the bench, with the bar directly above the contact point during your regular bench. Tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulder off the bench and retract them, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Use your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Maintain this tight body position throughout the movement.

You can take a standard bench grip, or shoulder width to focus on the triceps. The bar, wrist, and elbow should stay in line at all times. Focus on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart.

Drive the bar up with as much force as possible. The elbows should be tucked in until lockout.

Return the bar to the pins, pausing before beginning the next repetition.
